title: Illegal Instruction in streamlit versions newer than 0.84.2
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

On my system hardware any attempt to run streamlit newer than 0.84.2 results in "Illegal instruction", even when just running streamlit --version

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
No code needed, fails with streamlit hello or even streamlit --version
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Install streamlit 0.85 or newer on older hardware and run streamlit --version or streamlit hello

### Expected Behavior

Streamlit is the only application I can not run. I have compiled and installed current versions of the Apache web server, Python 3.11, OpenSSL 1.1.1s, and other modern applications successfully.

### Current Behavior

Any attempt to run streamlit newer than 0.84.2 produces an "Illegal instruction".

### Is this a regression?

- [X] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.85.0 or newer
- Python version: 3.9.16 and 3.11
- Operating System: OpenSuSE Linux
- Browser: N/A, all
- Virtual environment: N/A


### Additional Information

CPU info:

- [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The problem appears to be the new requirement for pyarrow. Every version of pyarrow I have tried so far from the latest version back to version 3.0.0 exits with an illegal instruction after installation as soon as I execute:
import pyarrow
version 2.0.0 and earlier of pyarrow fails to install.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
This seems to be a known bug in pyarrow:
[PYArrow build bug](https://github.com/conda-forge/pyarrow-feedstock/issues/84)
Is there am easy way to patch streamlit to optionally eliminate the requirement for pyarrow?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I successfully removed all references to pyarrow from my local copy of streamlit 1.18.1 and set the default for global.dataFrameSerialization to legacy and this fixed the issue. Everything I have tried so far works now. I think perhaps if pyarrow is to be supported it should be optional and detected if it is not present and streamlit should fall back to a global.dataFrameSerialization type of legacy. I have replicated this issue with pyarrow not building correctly now on a few different systems, including my 64 bit intel Mac and another Linux system. If streamlit is to be cross platform this should be seriously looked at.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
[streamlit-nopyarrow.patch](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/10779507/streamlit-nopyarrow.patch)
Until a more elegant solution is found, perhaps this patch will be useful to someone else...

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hello @reporter and thank you for opening this issue!

Our new features will heavily use pyarrow and it will get increasingly important, `dataFrameSerialization` `legacy` might be even removed in the future. 

So it would be great to try to have a working setup with pyarrow on your setup! 

Could you please describe more about this issue? 

Especially interesting is this part:

> I have replicated this issue with pyarrow not building correctly now on a few different systems, including my 64 bit intel Mac and another Linux system. If streamlit is to be cross platform this should be seriously looked at.

Do you use `conda`, does it work when you try to install streamlit via `pip`?

I am not sure about OpenSUSE, but streamlit definitely should work on Mac and most popular Linux distributives

comments.body:
This happens on (as I am finding out) quite a few systems.
[Arrow bug relating to older 64 bit CPUs](https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/21840)
I would definitely suggest taking this into account before eliminating "legacy" support. I am STILL trying to build pyarrow with this CPU acceleration support disabled.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: This may impact some virtual machine systems as well. :(

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: @participant1 just chiming in here from arrow to clarify. The problem is that arrow requires the `popcnt` instruction which was introduced ~2008. It seems some CPUs without this are still in use which then run into the Illegal Instruction exception. The possible fix is tracked here https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/23013

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I have been unable to build arrow from source to apply that fix after several attempts, plus that fix has not been included into the arrow code base yet. Additionally, I would like to point out that this can impact some installations on virtual machines. I have opened posted detailed information on this issue to the arrow github page. My first report was simply closed as a "won't fix". In my second report I pointed out that this can impact modern VMs and conflicts with the behavior described in their own documentation that says you can disable the use of SIMD CPU extensions. As I previously mentions, until the arrow project can fix this I would not abandon legacy support, in fact, a more elegant fix than my streamlit patch might be a good idea to allow steamlit to optionally disable arrow at runtime.

Perhaps something like:

```
import pyarrow as pa
try:
    pa.find_module('eggs')
    found = True
except ImportError:
    found = False
```
Then use the found flag variable to disable or change other sections of code so they work without arrow.

comments.body:
[streamlit-nopyarrow.patch](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/10819478/streamlit-nopyarrow.patch)
Here is a more elegant version of the patch I posted earlier. I am still testing this but it should be called the streamlit-detect-pyarrow.patch because it detects if pyarrow is not installed and changes to legacy mode if that is the case, otherwise it imports pyarrow and defaults to "arrow" mode.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: So I tested the hello app and a few other apps on a machine with this patch applient to streamlit 1.19 with pyarrow and a machine without pyarrow and it worked on both, automatically setting the default data serialization to arrow or falling back to legacy as appropriate.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I also submitted a patch to the apache arrow project which seems to fix pyarrow to work on older 64 bit CPUs like mine and on VMs that do not support certain CPU extensions. Hopefully they will incorporate it or something like it into their project soon. I have this patch working with pyarrow 4.0.1 currently, which meets streamlit's requirements for pyarrow.

https://github.com/apache/arrow/issues/34277

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I now have the patch for pyarrow working on version 5 of pyarrow. This is at least new enough to support streamlit, but I am not sure which systems my compiled copy will run on, besides mine. At the current time, anyone else with this issue would either have to patch streamlit to run without pyarrow, or build pyarrow from source code after applying my pyarrow patch.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have a python wheel of arrow version 5 that should work on many older Linux systems, but I can't attach it here as it is 49MB in size. The standard wheels from pypi are broken and use the popcnt. I also can't get any arrow version newer than 5 to compile on my system because while arrow is supposed to compile with gcc 7 (what I have), you actually need gcc 11  to build it. I am including a Google Drive link to the working python wheel, please archive it as I my not leave it up indefinitely as my Google storage is low on space. To install this wheel if you are running most Linux's and getting an illegal instruction from the pyarrow module download the whl file and run:
pip uninstall pyarrow
then
pip install pyarrow-5.0.0-cp39-cp39-linux_x86_64.whl

If this doesn't work on your server, leave me a message here and if I see it I'll try to help.

[PYArrow version 5.0.0 for linux, no CPU acceleration](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1q5V5V0beatqrqwUjGZE2ybA648yPqtCm?usp=sharing)

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Going to close this issue since a) as Karen outlined above, we increasingly rely on pyarrow under the hood. This is to make Streamlit faster (e.g. for `st.dataframe`) and allow it to handle much higher data loads. So making it optional in Streamlit is not possible. And b) the specific issue here seems to be a problem on the pyarrow side, so nothing we can fix or work around.

There's no working python 3.9 for Ubuntu 24 (bad move to be on the bleeding edge)... I tried to make it work on a docker image with python 3.9, I succeeded to install the prebuilt wheel for pyarrow 9 you provided, numpy 1.23.5 and streamlit, but then it starts complaining about libraries like libthrift-0.19.0.so and libc.so.6, which I wasn't able to make work, I think it's related to the docker operating system, or something... Conclusion, giving up again.
Thanks for all your help anyway Barry!
